title: Binary search
summary: Return the index of `target` in the sorted array `nums`, or -1 if it is not there.
hints: Look at the middle element first. Because the array is sorted, what does comparing it with the target tell you about half of the array?
Keep a low and a high position marking the part that could still contain the target. Each comparison with the middle lets you discard half of it.

While low <= high: mid = low + (high - low) / 2 using integer division. If nums[mid] is the target return mid; if it is smaller set low = mid + 1; otherwise set high = mid - 1. Return -1 after the loop.
takeaway: Halving the search range each step is O(log n): about 17 steps for 100,000 items. The classic bugs are an off-by-one in the loop condition and forgetting integer division for mid.
